x.ASV: A Song of Ascents. Behold, bless ye Jehovah, all ye servants of Jehovah, That by night stand in the house of Jehovah.
x.Darby: A Song of degrees. Behold, bless Jehovah, all ye servants of Jehovah, who by night stand in the house of Jehovah.
x.KJV: A Song of degrees. Behold, bless ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, which by night stand in the house of the Lord.
x.YLT: A Song of the Ascents. Lo, bless Jehovah, all servants of Jehovah, Who are standing in the house of Jehovah by night.

nt: The psalmist is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention]
The psalmist is speaking of the temple of Yahweh as if it were a **house** in which he lived. Alternate translation: [in the temple of Yahweh]

x.ASV: Lift up your hands to the sanctuary, And bless ye Jehovah.
x.Darby: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless Jehovah.
x.KJV: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord.
x.YLT: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, And bless ye Jehovah.

nt: To **Lift up** the **hands** was a symbolic action by which the Israelites showed their reverence and devotion to Yahweh in prayer. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation. Alternate translation: [Lift up your hands in prayer]

The word translated as **holiness** could refer to: (1) the holy place in the temple. Alternate translation: [to the holy place] or (2) the hands of the worshipers. Alternate translation: [in holiness]

x.ASV: Jehovah bless thee out of Zion; Even he that made heaven and earth.
x.Darby: Jehovah, the maker of heavens and earth, bless thee out of Zion.
x.KJV: The Lord that made heaven and earth bless thee out of Zion.
x.YLT: Jehovah doth bless thee out of Zion, The maker of the heavens and earth!

nt: The pronoun **you** here is singular and refers to each individual worshiper among the servants addressed earlier in this psalm. There the psalmist addressed the servants as a group using plural forms, but here the blessing shifts to the singular. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh bless each of you]

Here, **Zion** represents the place where Yahweh dwells among his people. The psalmist is using the name of this location to refer to God’s special presence there. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from his dwelling on Zion]

The psalmist is referring to all of creation by naming two extremes, **heaven** and **earth**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all things]
